resale_co.name: Certificate of Housing Inspection (Housing Occupancy Certificate)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Keansburg Code Enforcement and Construction Office
resale_co.lead_time: The inspection must be scheduled before the sale or occupancy.
requirements: Certificate of Housing Inspection application signed by the owner, buyer or agent, with seller and buyer details, number of bedrooms and occupants
Inspection by a municipal inspector; all violations corrected before occupancy unless written arrangements are made
Smoke and carbon monoxide detector inspection is done with the housing inspection (extra fee)
Close all UCC permits (listed as a violation item on the form)
Fire extinguisher (form still lists it as a violation item)
By signing for a sale, the owner or agent attests that no adjoining property is owned by the same person that may require a formal subdivision

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Housing Inspection Application and bring or mail it with payment to the Code Enforcement and Construction Office, Borough Hall, 29 Church Street, Keansburg, NJ 07734 (open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.). Applications must be submitted in person or by mail; no electronic submissions. Schedule the inspection before the sale or occupancy.

evidence.quote: Whenever there is a proposed change of ownership of any dwelling unit, such change of ownership shall not be made nor shall the subsequent owner occupy or permit occupancy of, nor shall any person rent, lease or occupy, the dwelling unit, without first complying with the requirements of this section.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code 11-3.1 (read through the ecode360 print view) requires a housing occupancy certificate before a change of ownership. Fee sources disagree: the 2023 application says $75.00 for two inspections plus $45 for the smoke/CO inspection (total $120); the Construction Office page lists '$120 will entitle the applicant to 2 (two) inspections' under its landlord registration section, with later reinspections at $30, $40, $70 and $100 per unit; the Code (11-3.1b) still says $75 plus $20 per later reinspection, and an older section (11-2.6) says $25. Confirm the current total with the office. Staff emails on the Borough page are hidden behind protected links. Staff listed: Paul Durnien, Construction Official (Ext. 220); Kathy Burgess, Zoning Official (Ext. 220); Chris Hoff, Code Enforcement Officer (Ext. 222); Arthur Boden, Fire Official (Ext. 224). The Borough moved its website to keansburgnj.gov; the old keansburg-nj.us address now shows a parked page. Landlord registration, vacant property registration and rooming house licensing are not resale requirements.

LEAID: 1321-001 Keansburg Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Keansburg Boro Code Enf Enf Auth. Fire Dept Fire Official Arthur V Boden Phone (732) 787-0215 Email arthur.boden@keansburg-nj.us

fire_cert.notes: Keansburg is its own fire code enforcing agency (LEA code F). The smoke/CO check is handled with the Borough housing inspection through the Code Enforcement and Construction Office, where Fire Official Arthur Boden is listed at Ext. 224. The 2023 application charges a flat $45 for the smoke/CO inspection, while Code 11-5 still lists $35 / $75 / $125 by business days before the change of occupancy; confirm which applies. The email comes from the state fire directory and uses the old keansburg-nj.us domain, which now shows a parked page, so it may not work. The form lists a fire extinguisher as a possible violation; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: The housing inspection form lists 'Close all UCC Permits' as a violation that must be corrected before occupancy.

other_items.label: Adjoining lots
other_items.detail: For a sale, the person signing the application attests that no adjoining property is owned by the same person that may require a formal subdivision before the sale.
